claims.text: Nonidentity bigrassmannians are parameterized by \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) with \(t>r+s-n\); \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) is the unique permutation with the stated descent conditions and \(v_t=s+1\), explicitly \[ (1,\ldots,t-1,\ s+1,\ldots,s+r-t+1,\ t,\ldots,s,\ s+r-t+2,\ldots,n). \] [source-2@L973-L993|claim=formal-document]

Set \(i=s-t+1\) and \(j=r-t+1\). The source says \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) corresponds to the \(j\times i\) rectangle \(i^j\); its theorem further assumes \(\schubp_v=s_{i^j}\). [source-2@L1354-L1362|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1380-L1387|claim=formal-document]

\(\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}(x_1,x_2,\ldots)\); \(I_{r,n-r}\) is the \(\mathbb Z\)-span of \(s_\lambda\) for \(\lambda\not\subseteq(n-r)^r\), and is an ideal. The source gives \[ \Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\cong \mathbb Z[\mathbf x]^{W_J}/\mathbb Z[\mathbf x]^W_+\mathbb Z[\mathbf x]^{W_J} \cong H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z). \] [source-2@L1310-L1330|claim=formal-document]

claims.text: In the supplied type-\(A\) material, \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is characterized as the ideal of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) generated by \[ \{\schubp_u:\Des(u)=\{(r,r+1)\},\,u\ge v_{r,s,t,n}\} =\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}. \] [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document]

For \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\), the theorem labelled `J-generators` gives the two ideal-generating sets \[ \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}, \qquad \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}. \] They generate \(J_v\) in \(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [source-2@L1380-L1402|claim=formal-document]

The source geometrically describes the first upper shape as adjoining an \(a\times b\) rectangle to the right of \(i^j\), top-justified, and the second as adjoining a \(b\times a\) rectangle below \(i^j\), left-justified. It states that each displayed generating set has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements and degree enumerator \(q^{ij}\qbin{a+b}{a}\). [source-2@L1407-L1421|claim=formal-document]

groundings.excerpt:
727:  Given $J \subset S$, one has the parabolic subgroup $W_J$ of $W$
728: generated by $J$.  One also has a corresponding parabolic subgroup $P_J$ of $G$,
729: generated by the Borel subgroup $B$ together with representatives within $G$
730: that lift the elements $J \subset W=N_G(T)/T$.
731: The Borel picture identifies the cohomology ring
732: of the {\bf (generalized) partial flag manifold}  $G/P_J$ as the subring of
733: $W_J$-invariants inside the cohomology of $G/B$.  In other words, 
734: the quotient map 
735: \[G/B \overset{\pi}{\rightarrow} G/P_J\] 
736: induces the inclusion
737: \begin{equation}
738: \label{parabolic-inclusion}
739: H^\star(G/P_J) \cong H^\star(G/B)^{W_J} \overset{i}{\hookrightarrow} H^\star(G/B).
740: \end{equation}
